text:
anna: heads up — after yesterday's canary we see a sustained 10-20% throughput drop on the mixed NF4/FP4 path and GPU memory looks fragmented over time :thinking:

matt: I noticed that in metrics. Any small logs or sample traces to start with? :eyes:

anna: pasting a short extract from the runtime monitor (30m window):
```
[2026-03-17 03:12:22] model=redwood/7B quant=NF4 kernel=quant4-4i batch=8 seq=512 alloc_failed=false
gpu_mem_free: 2.1GB -> 1.2GB (30m)
cuMalloc_count: 12489 -> 21543
eviction_rate_kv: 0.8% -> 2.6%
```

sasha: that cuMalloc delta + eviction delta smells like heap / slab fragmentation + many small device alloc/free pairs from batching. Did client batch size distribution change when we flipped clients to prefer FP4?

anna: yes — p50 batch size moved from 4 -> 6 after rollout (clients doing more dynamic chunking).

joel: also seeing KV cache churn in tracing: keys are getting evicted earlier, and compaction doesn't seem to kick in until memory pressure is high. Could be interplay between allocator and KV page lifetime.

perf-bot: daily perf digest: mixed-quant path regression flagged (score -12%) — report: http://perf.local/reports/21876 (internal)

matt: quick local experiment: forcing max_batch=8 reduces the small-allocation churn (fewer cuMalloc calls) but end-to-end p99 latency increases. So batching heuristic is oscillating between cost and latency.

sasha: proposal: 1) add an aggregator for small device allocations (sub-4k pages) to avoid repeated cuMalloc/cuFree; 2) add a background KV compaction pass (every 5m) to coalesce pages; 3) add a pre-allocated slab for hot-kv pages.

anna: sounds good. I want a profiling capture before we change allocator behavior to prove causality. Who can run a 2-hour nvprof + host malloc histogram?

joel: I can. Will run pprof + nvprof sampling starting 10:00 PT and collect:
```
./capture_pprof --duration=7200 --nvprof --collect-host-malloc-hist --out=pprof_21876.tar.gz
```
I'll also capture device malloc/free stack traces and allocation size histogram.

matt: add a microbenchmark too: steady stream of short requests (seq=32) across NF4 and FP4 kernels to try to reproduce cuMalloc churn locally. If churn reproduces there, easier to iterate.

anna: agreed. If we confirm fragmentation is the root cause, rollout plan: backport slab-aggregator + limit dynamic batch p50->6 for 48h as temporary mitigation.

sasha: one more note — the calibration pass introduced for FP4 mixed mode spawns ephemeral re-embedding buffers in some code paths. Those buffers might not be pooled and could exacerbate fragmentation; check calibration hooks.

anna: good catch. Please add a check in the calibration code to reuse temp buffers (or use pre-allocated buffer arena) as part of the repro.

infra-bot: pinging infra on-call @infra-team for visibility and possible allocator kernel support.

anna: assign @joel to INF-5473 and I'll attach the perf digest + nvprof tar when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:

joel: starting capture now, will post results + flamegraphs here when available. :mag_right:
